title: Kunneth for cohomology with closed support
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an integer $n\geq1$, put
$A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and let $Z\subset X,W\subset Y$
be closed subschemes of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes.
Let $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D^b(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be
bounded complexes,
with $L$ of
finite Tor amplitude.
Then the supported
exterior product is an isomorphism:

$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:
R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

Here $R\Gamma_Z,R\Gamma_W$ are the
derived support functors.
The assertion also holds for the pro-etale realizations of these
complexes equipped with
etale-origin witnesses.

proof.text: Finite-type schemes over the field are locally Noetherian. Their open complements are quasi-compact, and their structural maps and the product projections remain separated and finite type. The Lean proof uses the corresponding existing scheme instances. The proved estimate [lem-pur-supported-product-bounded-below] supplies a lower bound for each external product needed for localization; the same estimate applies after restricting K to an open subset. No separate choice of a lower K-flat representative is needed. Exact projection and open inverse image use [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

source.place: Paragraphs 1-4; Lean proof using the normalized localization maps

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] in the second variable, with full first support. Its middle and open components are the supported products with full supports, followed in the open component by the specified invertible support transport. By [lem-pur-supported-full-support-product] these are invertible from [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring], applied to the original scheme pair and the pair with the open complement of W. The characteristic of D.k equals D.p: its finite subfield has cardinality a power of D.p, and algebraic field extension preserves characteristic. Thus the coefficient-prime hypothesis of ordinary Kunneth holds. Two-out-of-three [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the intersection component invertible. Cancel its specified support congruence and apply [lem-pur-supported-product-support-congruence] to replace the intersection of the identity support with j by j. This proves the product for full first support and arbitrary second support. Products throughout are those of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product].

source.place: Paragraphs 1-4; Lean proof using the normalized localization maps

proof.text: Repeat this second-variable argument with the open complement of Z in place of X and the exact restriction of K. Apply [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] in the first variable, with full ambient support and closed support i. The middle and open components are invertible by the preceding argument. Two-out-of-three [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] gives the intersection component. Cancel its specified invertible support transport. The intersection of the identity support with i has exactly the open complement of i, so [lem-pur-supported-product-support-congruence] gives invertibility of the actual product for i,j. This is the blueprint double localization, including the prescribed boundary maps.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-4; Lean proof using the normalized localization maps

proof.text: Package the bounded complexes K,L as bounded-below objects. Their external product is bounded below by [lem-pur-supported-product-bounded-below]. For canonical comparison pullbacks apply the exterior equality of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]. Its three support comparison maps are invertible: each is the composite of a kernel-evaluation isomorphism, the right-derived/plus compatibility isomorphisms, and the invertible bounded-below support comparison. All external coefficient comparisons and the etale supported product are invertible. Consequently the composite of the tensor of the two comparisons with the pro-etale product is invertible, and cancellation gives invertibility of the canonical pro-etale product.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-4; Lean proof using the normalized localization maps

proof.text: For a specified [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], the comparison pullback of K is isomorphic to its fixed-ring pro-etale realization: first apply comparison pullback to the inverse of the supplied origin isomorphism, then the unit of the realization-derived equivalence, then its inverse functor applied to the derived-composite comparison and the supplied witness alpha. Do this for K and L. The proved naturality lemma [lem-pur-proetale-supported-product-naturality] transfers invertibility from the canonical comparison pullbacks to these two specified objects. This proves the universal witness clause without choosing new origin data.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-4; Lean proof using the normalized localization maps

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1-4. Same double-localization route, with a proved abstract Tor estimate and proved witness naturality; full-support and support-presentation normalization are isolated as independent results.
